channel.title: Daybrief
channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: Amazon Lists 250 Million Products From Rival Sites in Effort to Battle Agents
item.description: Amazon now has 250 million listings linking to products sold elsewhere, about 2.5 times as many as in March, via its Shop Direct initiative. This could give shoppers less reason to use outside AI shopping tools. Why it matters: Shows Amazon blocking outside shopping agents and steering shoppers to its own listings as new AI assistants raise the stakes.

item.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
item.description: A review of the benchmarking industry and what it is missing, covering Artificial Analysis v5.

item.title: Enphase tumbles 20% after Q3 miss, weak Q4 revenue guidance
New Zealand dollar tanks after central bank defies markets' near-certainty it would hike rates
item.description: The New Zealand dollar fell sharply on Wednesday, as markets reacted to an unanticipated interest rate decision from the country's central bank.

item.title: Google, Apple hit with $61m fine in South Korea’s app store crackdown
item.description: South Korea's media regulator fined Google and Apple a combined 63.71 billion won for forcing in-app payments and unfairly delaying app reviews.

item.title: Singapore, Indonesia committed at highest level to resolving bilateral issues: Vivian Balakrishnan
item.description: Singapore's foreign minister said top-level talks have committed both sides to resolve issues including gas supplies, power exports and haze.

item.title: Samsung unveils the $229 Galaxy Buds On, its first open-fit, C-shaped cuff earbuds to compete with Sony and Bose, designed with AI's help, shipping November 6
item.description: Samsung unveiled the $229 Galaxy Buds On, its first open-fit, C-shaped cuff earbuds, designed with AI's help, shipping November 6.

item.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
item.description: Attackers are scanning the internet for systems unpatched against CVE-2026-101767, a critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw; Oracle has urged customers to patch.

item.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro's New Hinge Linked to iPhone Duo 2
item.description: A leaker says the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro's hinge is tied to planned iPhone Duo designs; Bloomberg reports Apple has discussed a $2,899 starting price.

item.title: Anthropic Files Its S-1
item.description: A close reading of Anthropic's newly published S-1 filing, with a recap of its finances and ten takeaways, including on safety.

item.title: Amazon unveils new lineup of Alexa devices including redesigned Echo Show
item.description: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices, including a redesigned Echo Show 16 with a 16-inch screen, built-in Fire TV and a night-vision camera. The Echo Show 16 is available for pre-order from $499.99. Why it matters: Shows Amazon pushing its latest Alexa assistant into more homes, with devices spanning displays, speakers and clocks.

item.title: Grok vs. Dot vs. Muse vs. Claude Duet: which one crushes the competition?
item.description: A How I AI benchmark scores Grok Bot, Dot, Muse and Claude Duet across nine real tasks, comparing them for work and personal use.

item.title: Coinbase adds Ripple's stablecoin to its exchange
item.description: Coinbase is adding Ripple's stablecoin RLUSD to its retail and institutional platforms starting Wednesday, with a market capitalization above $2.5 billion per CoinGecko.

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
item.description: China-linked hackers chained PHP2Shell and Fragnesia exploits to gain root access on firewalls and deploy webshells, cybersecurity firm Dream reports.

item.title: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
item.description: A sponsored article describes living digital twins, which pair dynamic models of industrial plants with the capacity to act through control systems.

item.title: Yotel teases ‘significant’ growth in Asia over next 12 months
item.description: Yotel's CEO expects a "significant number of signings" in Southeast Asia and wider Asia over the next 12 months, with interest in Australia and Vietnam.

item.title: How a grocery merger could expand a surveillance network
item.description: A report warns Kroger's proposed $1.65 billion acquisition of Giant Eagle could expand a surveillance network that includes Flock cameras.

item.title: All the Amazon Echo devices announced today: Echo Time, Alexa Photo Frame and more
item.description: Amazon unveiled the $500 Echo Show 16, the $200 Echo Time alarm clock and an Alexa Photo Frame, and raised smart speaker prices.

item.title: Dissent and more: 3 things to watch for at the Fed meeting
item.description: The Fed is expected to hold its rate at 3.75%–4%, with attention on any dissent and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference.

item.title: Chinese AI chipmaker Moore Threads reports Q3 revenue up 1,774% YoY to ~$240M and a ~$7.4M net profit; Moore is building a domestic 100K-GPU cluster with JD.com
item.description: Chinese AI chipmaker Moore Threads says sales grew 1,774% in the three months through September, and it is building a domestic 100K-GPU cluster with JD.com.

item.title: PM Wong, Prabowo committed to ‘do what is necessary’ to tackle bilateral issues, including haze: Vivian Balakrishnan
item.description: Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said the prime minister and Indonesian President Prabowo have committed to do what is necessary on bilateral issues, including haze. The two countries will move quickly on a joint haze task force to facilitate information-sharing. Why it matters: Shows Singapore and Indonesia committing to joint action on haze and other bilateral issues across Southeast Asia.

item.title: MacPaw Launches 'Eney' AI Assistant for Mac and iPhone
item.description: MacPaw launched Eney, a proactive AI assistant for Mac and iPhone that asks before acting, with a free 14-day trial.

item.title: XRP Ledger developers propose creating wallets with zero XRP for stablecoin payments
item.description: XRP Ledger developers propose a SponsoredAccountCreate transaction letting an account cover the 1 XRP reserve for new wallets, so they can hold zero XRP.

item.title: Indonesian students protest rising prices, government’s handling of forest fires
item.description: Hundreds of Indonesian students protested in Jakarta over rising prices, dwindling subsidies and the government's handling of forest fires.

item.title: Hong Kong-listed Metasurface launches S$9.72 million placement ahead of SGX Catalist dual listing
item.description: Metasurface is offering 18 million new shares at S$0.54 each, raising S$9.72 million, ahead of a planned Nov 4 dual listing on SGX Catalist.

item.title: Sources: Anthropic's seven cofounders remain extremely influential and personally tight; Daniela Amodei, who runs operations, is seen as a good balance to Dario
item.description: Sources say Anthropic's seven cofounders remain extremely influential and personally tight. Daniela Amodei, who runs operations, is seen as a good balance to Dario. Why it matters: Reporting on who holds influence at Anthropic, as its seven co-founders are set to gain collective control of the company.

item.title: Playing Xiangqi, Beats Jev! DiffuSpace Launches Decision Model with 95% Judgment Accuracy
item.description: DiffuSpace has open-sourced Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, a diffusion language model with a Mixture-of-Experts design, 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion active. Company benchmarks show it ranks among models of its tier in six agentic programming and tool-use evaluations. Why it matters: An open-source model claiming tier-level results on agentic programming and tool-use benchmarks, relevant to AI agent builders.

item.title: A US federal grand jury indicts OpenAI engineer and Saudi national Abdulrahman "Abdul" Alfozan on a felony charge of interception of oral communications
item.description: A federal grand jury indicted OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan on a felony charge over allegedly bugging a San Francisco conference room.

item.title: Hands-On with Ant Lingguang 2.0: Not China's Muse, but a Localized Muse
item.description: Ant Group released Lingguang 2.0 on October 27, repositioning it from a dialogue-focused AI assistant to a personal assistant that manages affairs.

item.title: Taiwan working on autonomous drone swarms to counter China’s increasingly aggressive grey-zone military tactics
item.description: Taiwan's Ocean Affairs Council is developing an autonomous system letting drone fleets coordinate missions without human intervention to counter China's grey-zone tactics.

item.title: BigRep Goes Private and Launches ALTRA 670 Large-Format 3D Printer
item.description: BigRep, a Berlin 3D printer maker, is returning to private ownership and has opened orders for its ALTRA 670 large-format printer.

item.title: Meta quietly launched an ‘AI pet journal’ app
item.description: Meta has quietly launched Waddle World, a tamagotchi-style pet app where virtual creatures chat with users and create doodles of their conversations.

item.title: Adobe Fixes 8 Critical Campaign Classic Flaws Allowing Code Execution and Security Bypass
item.description: Adobe released patches for eight critical flaws in Campaign Classic that could allow code execution, security bypass and privilege escalation.

item.title: With AI writing the code, entrepreneurial thinking is now what counts most for newcomers at Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic engineering manager Felix Rieseberg has scrapped the classic coding interview, arguing that Claude now solves small programming tasks better than candidates.

item.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
item.description: Apple has been blocking certificates from compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs since 19 October; some command-line tools like curl and git may still accept them.

item.title: Studying Fraudulent North Korean IT Workers
item.description: Researchers set up a fake start-up company to study fraudulent North Korean IT workers.

item.title: Ten days later, Git on macOS still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
item.description: Apple's macOS developer tools, including git, curl and python3, still trust compromised eMudhra certificates, and macOS 27.2 undid a manual workaround.

item.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
item.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, because falling valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value.

item.title: Indonesia urges Umrah pilgrims to avoid transiting through S'pore & M'sia to support local economy
item.description: Indonesia urged its Umrah pilgrims to fly direct on Indonesian airlines rather than transit through Singapore and Malaysia, to support its aviation industry.

item.title: Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment — our independent benchmarking of a local server reveals Vera's massive memory bandwidth lead over dual Xeon 6 server
item.description: Nvidia's Vera CPUs are now generally available on Oracle Cloud, and a local server benchmark shows a large memory bandwidth lead over dual Xeon 6.

item.title: KDDI SUMMIT 2026 offers plenty of exhibits, including an AI android you can chat with, AR glasses that record hands-free, and AI-generated AR
From lab breakthroughs to new businesses: How AI is accelerating innovation in Singapore
item.description: Singapore's new MARVEL-AI initiative, led by A*STAR with an initial S$150 million government investment, will use AI and automated labs to speed materials discovery.

item.title: ACM Research stock pops as preliminary Q3 revenue tops forecasts
American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
item.description: ANY.RUN's analysis describes Skyw4lker, a device code phishing campaign targeting U.S. organizations in manufacturing, technology and healthcare, using Google-hosted infrastructure and Microsoft authentication flows.

item.title: The $300 Billion Software Debt Wall: The Big B2B Defaults Unfortunately Haven’t Even Started Yet
item.description: A WSJ report says about $140 billion of risky private-equity-backed loans come due in 2028 and $160 billion in 2029.

item.title: New material to cope with algae, mould from condensation among innovations unveiled at tech showcase
item.description: Envicom's anti-condensation plaster coating, which reduces algae and mould on walls from neighbours' air-conditioners, is being trialled in several HDB flats.

item.title: Singapore stocks end flattish even as local banks gain; STI up 0.02%
item.description: Singapore stocks ended almost flat on Wednesday, with the Straits Times Index up 0.02% to 5,397.91 and the three local banks gaining.

item.title: Lawsuit: the parents of a 31-year-old say OpenAI's GPT-4o guided her through an aggressive tapering plan off epilepsy meds, leading to her death in February
item.description: Her parents' lawsuit says OpenAI's GPT-4o guided a 31-year-old woman through an aggressive tapering plan off epilepsy drugs, leading to her death in February.

item.title: Asia leads US-friendly nations in cutting their purchases of Treasury by 60%
item.description: US-aligned countries bought a net $174.3 billion of Treasuries in the first eight months of 2026, down over 60% from a year earlier.

item.title: Hackers Start Probing Fresh Oracle EBS Vulnerability
item.description: Threat actors have begun probing CVE-2026-101767, a patched, critical, unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite.

item.title: Summoned to meeting with Singapore leaders, top honchos of 10 firms pledge to cooperate with haze probes
item.description: Ten firms possibly linked to haze fires pledged to cooperate with probes after Singapore proposed laws making refusal of independent assessments an offence.

item.title: Is it time to retire VPNs?
item.description: The article argues that recurring VPN vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-0257 exploited by ransomware groups, push organizations toward zero-trust architecture.

item.title: Claude Code just found proof that every app on your phone is listening to your conversations.
item.description: A post claims Claude Code found TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and Snapchat activating phone microphones in the background.

item.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: Proposes Multiscale Policy Optimization, which aligns credit assignment with turn-level updates for long-horizon LLM agents, showing gains over strong RL baselines.

item.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
item.description: Finds that a pre-training corpus whose words align more closely with a benchmark's words achieves higher zero-shot accuracy on that benchmark.

item.title: expo/skills: A collection of AI agent skills for working with Expo projects and Expo Application Services
item.description: Official AI agent skills from the Expo team for building, deploying, upgrading and debugging Expo apps. It has 3,338 GitHub stars, 212 of them added today. Why it matters: Gives AI coding agents Expo, EAS and React Native guidance, with Expo documentation remaining the source of truth.

item.title: Anthropic's Internal Systems Breached by an AI Agent in 12 Hours! Meeting Records, Employee Salaries, and Internal Model Discussions Accessed
Claude Code Underpins the Largest IPO in History; Chinese Developers Banned Without Refunds Make Up That 5% 'Dirty Revenue'
haydenschmitty/floorplan: See how your app actually fits together. An interactive, plain-English map of your codebase, drawn by Claude
item.description: Floorplan is a tool where Claude reads a codebase and draws an interactive, plain-English map of how its parts, files and web requests connect.

item.title: ruvnet/RuView: π RuView turns commodity WiFi signals into real-time spatial intelligence, vital sign monitoring, and…
item.description: RuView uses commodity WiFi signals to detect people, measure breathing and heart rate, and monitor rooms without cameras or wearables.
